query: What simulation-based power analysis and model-recovery pipeline will determine trial counts and expected detectability of time-varying parameters in hierarchical effort models?

response.query: What simulation-based power analysis and model-recovery pipeline will determine trial counts and expected detectability of time-varying parameters in hierarchical effort models?
response.answer: The simulation-based power analysis and model-recovery pipeline uses Monte Carlo simulations to determine trial counts and expected detectability of time-varying parameters in hierarchical effort models. It leverages statistical inference and resampling techniques for robust analysis.

results.content: Additionally, we utilize the Monte Carlo model of polarized light transfer to model the interaction of the polarized light with optical phantom for both a back-reflected MM and confocal Mueller Matrix imaging to validate our findings. Author(s): Meishu Wang, MOE Key Laboratory of Optoelectronic Imaging Technology and System, Beijing Institute of Technology (China), LPICM, CNRS, Ecole Polytechnique, IP Paris (France); Sooyong Chae, Théotim Lucas, Lab. de Physique des Interfaces et des Couches Minces, CNRS (France), École Polytechnique, Institut Polytechnique de Paris (France); Omar Rodríguez-Núñez, Inselspital (Switzerland); Éléa Romy Gros, Christopher Hahne, Theoni Maragkou, Richard McKinley, Univ. Polarized light is sensitive to the optical anisotropy of white matter, caused by densely packed myelinated fibers, and can enhance contrast in polarimetric images of linear retardance and optical axis azimuth. Our findings bridge structured light optics and biomedical imaging and suggest that OAM-based modalities can complement polarization-sensitive diagnostics.
